notes: Accept, with three titles corrected in place. The recorded hash of the published Acta PDF reproduces (0d81a6d3…) and I re-extracted all 56 pages, printed pages 103–158. Structure: 136 items (119 missing, 12 planned, 5 library), every missing item routed exactly once, both source stages exist, all twelve planned layer ids exist, all four Part II parents exist, all four areas are galaxy ids, and check_paper.py passes; the planned items named inside the source routes are the provision of PROTOCOL §16. All eight declarations behind the five library items resolve at the pins: Derivation, IsAzumaya with AlgHom.mulLeftRight, WittVector with ext, frobeniusEquiv with coeff_frobenius_charP, and WittVector.Isocrystal. The corrections are the Part II titles. PROTOCOL §16 asks the proposed title to be '<parent title>, Part II: <topic>', and three of the four paraphrased their parent: 'Semisimple algebras, Artin–Wedderburn and module structure' for the atlas's 'Semisimple algebras, Artin-Wedderburn, and the structure of their modules'; 'Crystalline cohomology' for 'Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations'; and 'P-adic differential equations and rigid cohomology' for 'P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights'. Each of those three ids is proposed by this extraction alone, so restoring the parent titles breaks nothing; the fourth, HodgeStructuresPartII, already matched and is shared with three other extractions, which is how I checked that the convention is exactness rather than paraphrase. All ten findings are confirmed at their locators in the published text. E1 is the clearest: p.106 defines cohomological rigidity by H¹_dR(X,(End(E),∇)) = 0 while p.148 uses End⁰, and on a fixed-determinant moduli space the trace-free version is the one that matches 'reduced isolated point'. E4 is of the same kind at Definition 5.2, where Def_ϱ carries no determinant condition although the rest of the paper fixes the determinant. E2's uniqueness claim rests on monicity, which does not give uniqueness of a factorisation over a non-reduced base. E3, E5 and E6 are gaps of the shape recorded: an (m−1)-truncation need not keep the order of the Hitchin invariant; vanishing after restriction does not localise a form to the zero-section; and vanishing of gr(∇_s) at good points of infinitely many fibres needs the shrinking of S that the correction supplies. E7 through E10 are printed as quoted, including 'integrality condition' for integrability and Ω¹_X for Ω¹_Z on p.108, and the C₁/C₁^{−1} clash between Definition 4.1(b) and (c). I checked every finding at its locator and the definitions each one turns on; I did not re-derive the paper's main theorems, and I add no finding.
